newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen indices edge lower at noon on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen indices edge lower at noon on correction.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices ended Wednesday morning slightly lower as investors took advantage of recent rallies and extended profit-taking that began on Tuesday, analysts said.
The markets were likely to extend narrow-band fluctuations in the afternoon as investors waited for fresh news related to listed firms' interim results, they said.

The hard currency B share index edged down 0.73 points or 0.55 percent to 132.08 points on thin turnover of HK$11.5 million. The Chinese yuan-based A share index shaved 3.58 points or 0.87 percent to 409.56 on turnover of 3.8 billion yuan.
"The falls are largely technical. There is a lack of trading incentive," a trader at China Guotai Securities said.
"I think the indices are going to fluctuate in a thin band as investors adopt a wait-and-see attitude," the trader said.
First half reports are becoming the market talking point in the run-up to the August 31 publication deadline, and the indices have rallied on buying of firms expected to post good results.
"Today has been a quiet day as we are looking for fresh information about company reports after the recent rebound," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
In the B share market, colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics Co Ltd was the biggest loser, sliding HK$0.28 or 8.54 percent to HK$3.00.
In the A share market, property concern Guizhou Zhongtian (Group) was the worst performer and lost 0.91 yuan or 6.97 percent to 12.15 yuan.
